stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Agronomists studying wheat farms in the Palouse region long assumed that growers would be ______ no-till planting. They expected farmers to balk at the price of specialized seed drills and at the risk of lower yields during the first few seasons. A 2021 survey of 400 farms complicated that assumption: nearly 60 percent of respondents had already adopted the method on at least part of their land.
explanation: The blank is part of the old assumption that the survey later overturns. The next sentence explains that assumption: farmers were expected to 'balk at' the cost and the risk. Balking at a new practice means being reluctant to adopt it, so 'resistant to' is the right description of the expected attitude toward no-till planting.

A.why: You picked a strong, vivid reaction that fits the topic. Balking at a cost means hesitating, not being furious, so 'outraged by' claims far more emotion than the text supports.

B.why: You may have read the survey result into the blank. The blank belongs to the earlier assumption, which expected farmers to balk, and that is the opposite of being eager.

D.why: You chose a phrase about ability when the text describes attitude. The expectation was about whether farmers would want to adopt the method because of cost and risk, not whether they knew how to do it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Labor economist Renata Okafor found that machinists laid off from automotive plants were often ______ publicly funded retraining programs: fewer than one in five of the workers she tracked enrolled, even when tuition was fully covered, and many told her they doubted a new credential would lead to wages comparable to those they had lost.
explanation: The text after the colon defines the blank. Few workers enrolled even though it was free, and many 'doubted' the programs would pay off. Doubting whether something is worth it means being 'skeptical of' it.

B.why: You went for the strongest emotion on the list. The workers expressed doubt, not anger, and nothing in the text suggests they were furious.

C.why: You chose a phrase about eligibility, but the explanation after the colon is about the workers' doubts. Being qualified for a program says nothing about why so few chose to enroll.

D.why: You matched the free tuition instead of the workers' reaction to it. Low enrollment and open doubt point the opposite way from gratitude.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Having spent decades shaping soda-lime glass, the artisans at the Carrow Street workshop were initially ______ borosilicate, a glass that softens only at much higher temperatures and so demands different timing at the torch. As a result, many of the first vessels they made from it came out cracked or lopsided.
explanation: The artisans' long practice was with a different glass, borosilicate requires different timing, and their first pieces failed. All three point to a lack of practice with the new material, and 'initially' signals that this changed later. 'Inexperienced with' describes that situation.

A.why: You may have attached 'decades' to the wrong glass. Their decades of experience were with soda-lime glass. The cracked first vessels show they were not yet used to borosilicate.

B.why: You picked a vivid reaction to explain the failed pieces. The text explains the failures with technique and timing, not with any strong dislike of the material.

C.why: You chose a phrase about interest when the text is about experience. Nothing suggests the artisans did not care about borosilicate. The problem was that they had not yet mastered it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: It may seem that a discipline as dependent on costly instruments as astronomy would be ______ contributions from amateurs. In fact, professional research teams increasingly rely on hobbyists with backyard telescopes, who have timed thousands of stellar occultations and flagged dozens of previously unknown supernovae.
explanation: 'It may seem' introduces an impression, and 'In fact' reverses it. The reality is that professionals rely on amateurs, so the impression in the blank must be the opposite: a field that does not accept outside help. 'Closed to' describes that lack of openness.

A.why: You were drawn to a strong negative phrase. The reversal only needs a lack of openness. Nothing suggests anyone would be angry about amateur help, so 'furious at' goes too far.

C.why: You put the real situation into the blank. The blank sits inside the view that 'In fact' knocks down, so it has to be the opposite of welcoming.

D.why: You chose a phrase about ability, but the contrast is about openness, meaning whether the field accepts amateurs' work. 'Skilled in contributions' also does not describe that relationship.

explanation: The phrase after the comma defines the blank. The forecasters kept using the old system until the new model 'had proved itself.' Holding back trust until something earns it is caution, so 'wary of' fits.

B.why: The forecasters watched the new model's performance through a full season before trusting it, so they clearly knew it existed.

D.why: You took the end of the story for the beginning. The text says they began to depend on the model only after 2020. In 2019 they were still basing warnings on the older system.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Folklorist Ines Varga expected the older storytellers of a mountain village in northern Romania to refuse to be recorded, since several had turned away researchers in the 1970s. explanation: The word "Instead" tells you the storytellers did not refuse as expected. The text after the colon then describes the response: few volunteered, but most agreed once the archive was explained. That is willingness to go along, not eagerness. "Receptive to" names exactly that kind of openness.

A.why: You went with the expectation that "Instead" knocks down. Being suspicious of the project is close to refusing, and the passage says most storytellers agreed to be recorded.

C.why: You picked the vivid, positive phrase because the reaction was positive. But "few volunteered on their own" rules out excitement. They were open, not delighted.

D.why: Nothing in the passage is about whether the storytellers understood recording. The blank describes how they reacted to the project, and being unfamiliar with it says nothing about that reaction.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Because the charge-coupled device cameras used at professional observatories cost more than a small car until the early 1990s, most amateur astronomers remained ______ digital imaging for decades. explanation: "Because" ties the blank to cost. The cameras were too expensive, so amateurs never got to use them. They sketched by hand until prices fell. What follows from that is a lack of hands-on experience, which is what "inexperienced with" means.

A.why: You missed the direction of the cause. If amateurs could not afford the cameras and sketched by hand instead, they could not have become skilled at digital imaging.

B.why: You chose a feeling that suits the topic. The passage never says amateurs used digital imaging and found it lacking. They simply had no access to it.

C.why: You read cost as resistance. The passage gives price as the only barrier and shows amateurs taking up imaging once it was affordable, so there is no sign they objected to it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Music historians have long described the German organist Matthias Brenner (1681–1744) as hostile to the Italian operatic style that was spreading north in his lifetime. They show Brenner to have been ______ the style: he copied out dozens of Italian arias for private study, even while warning his students against imitating them wholesale.
explanation: The letters "complicate" the old view of Brenner, so the blank has to move away from hostility without going too far the other way. Copying arias for private study shows real interest. Warning students against wholesale imitation shows he held back from embracing the style. "Curious about" fits both halves.

B.why: You jumped from "not hostile" to the strongest positive phrase available. Someone devoted to the style would not warn students against imitating it, so this ignores the second half of the evidence.

C.why: This is the view the passage knocks down. The new letters "complicate that picture," so the blank cannot just repeat it.

D.why: Copying dozens of arias for study is the opposite of indifference. He was paying close attention to the style.

explanation: The second sentence defines the blank. The farmers had planted these varieties and could describe how they performed, so they had firsthand knowledge of them. A.why: Nearly nine in ten had planted these varieties and could describe their results. They clearly knew about them.

B.why: Fewer than one in five planted the varieties every year. Most farmers were clearly not relying on them.

stimulus: Coastal charts made by the Lisbon chartmakers' guild in the late 1600s show mapmakers who were ______ secondhand reports from sailors. explanation: The second sentence shows what the mapmakers did with sailors' reports. They used them, but only after confirmation, and they flagged anything unconfirmed. Accepting information while checking it carefully is what "cautious about" means.

A.why: Requiring a second captain's confirmation and labeling unconfirmed islands are signs of care. The passage shows the reverse of carelessness.

C.why: You read their checking as rejection. The mapmakers still added confirmed shoals and still recorded unconfirmed islands as "reported," so they did not dismiss the reports. They handled them carefully.

D.why: The mapmakers handled sailors' reports routinely. They compared them and labeled them, so they knew these reports well.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Sports scientists had expected veteran distance runners to dismiss unfamiliar recovery techniques, assuming that athletes with decades of training habits would hold on to the routines that had served them. A 2023 survey of 400 such runners found otherwise: most described themselves as ______ new methods, and nearly two-thirds had tried at least one, such as cold-water immersion or sleep tracking, in the previous year, even when the benefits were uncertain.
explanation: The colon tells you that what follows explains the blank. The runners tried new methods even when the benefits were uncertain, which reverses the expectation that they would dismiss them. That points to a willingness to try new things. "Receptive to" means open to, so it matches both the reversal and the evidence.

A.why: You treated trying a method as mastering it. The survey says the runners experimented with new techniques, not that they became skilled at them, so "proficient in" describes ability when the passage only supports openness.

C.why: You missed the word "otherwise." Runners who sought out new methods and tried them despite uncertain benefits are not indifferent. "Indifferent to" comes close to the expectation the survey disproved.

D.why: You picked the most vivid phrase for the positive direction. Trying one technique in a year shows openness, not fixation, so "obsessed with" is far stronger than the evidence allows.

stimulus: Unlike the excavation's senior staff, most of the volunteers who joined the 2019 dig at the hillfort were ______ stratigraphic recording. D.why: You imagined how beginners might feel and picked a strong emotion. The passage describes only what the volunteers didn't yet know, not how they reacted, so "frustrated by" goes beyond the evidence.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Some critics assume that eighteenth-century concertgoers expected performers to play a score exactly as written. One musicologist argues instead that these listeners were ______ improvisation. Concert reports from the period describe soloists freely ornamenting repeated passages as a matter of course, and the writers mention the practice without comment, as they would any ordinary feature of a performance.
explanation: The blank sits in the view that reverses the critics' assumption. The evidence is that improvisation happened "as a matter of course" and was mentioned "without comment," which describes something routine and familiar. "Accustomed to" fits that because it means used to something, without adding any strong feeling.

A.why: You saw that the relationship was positive and reached for the most vivid phrase. The reports mention ornamentation "without comment," which is the opposite of excitement, so "captivated by" is much stronger than the evidence supports.

B.why: You kept the critics' assumption instead of the musicologist's reversal. Listeners who treated ornamentation as ordinary were not disturbed by it, so "unsettled by" contradicts the evidence.

D.why: You confused the listeners with the performers. The soloists did the improvising. The passage says nothing about audiences having musical training, so "trained in" claims a skill the text never gives them.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Many nineteenth-century surveyors treated residents' accounts of a landscape as hearsay to be corrected by instruments. Cartographer Annika Velde, by contrast, was notably ______ local knowledge: while mapping a shifting river delta, she hired fishers as guides, asked them which channels silted up each season, and recorded their names for the waterways alongside her own measurements.
explanation: Two things set the answer. "By contrast" means Velde's attitude is the opposite of treating local accounts as hearsay, and the text after the colon shows what that attitude looked like: she hired local guides, asked them questions, and recorded their names. That is openness. "Receptive to" means willing to take in and consider something, which matches both clues.

A.why: You described the other surveyors, not Velde. "By contrast" tells you she differed from colleagues who brushed off residents' accounts, and hiring fishers as guides is the opposite of being dismissive.

C.why: You read the blank as a skill when the passage describes an attitude. Velde isn't trying to have local knowledge herself. She is choosing to seek it out and use it, so how practiced she is doesn't come into it.

D.why: You picked the strongest phrase that fits the topic. The colon shows practical steps, like hiring guides and writing down names, which show openness. Nothing shows fascination or delight, so "enthralled by" claims more than the text supports.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: A new magnesium alloy is lighter than the aluminum used in most aircraft, but it has been through only six months of stress testing. Aircraft engineers have therefore been ______ the material. Expecting that years of repeated loading might expose flaws the short trials missed, they have approved it for cabin fittings while continuing to build load-bearing parts from aluminum.
explanation: "Therefore" ties the engineers' attitude to the limited testing, and the next sentence shows that attitude in action. They allow the alloy where failure would do little harm but keep it out of load-bearing parts. That is a measured, careful response, neither a rejection nor full trust. "Cautious about" names it precisely.

A.why: You chose a strong negative phrase because the engineers are holding back. But they did approve the alloy for cabin fittings, which rules out hostility. Their reluctance is limited, so "hostile to" overstates it.

B.why: You focused on the alloy's advantage and skipped the logic. "Therefore" follows from the short testing period, and keeping the alloy out of load-bearing parts shows doubt, not confidence.

D.why: You took the restrictions as a lack of interest. But the engineers weighed the alloy's risks and approved it for some uses, which shows active attention. Holding back out of care is not the same as not caring.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: When power looms arrived in the mills of Lowell, Massachusetts, in the 1820s, owners did not recruit the handloom weavers whose trade the machines replaced. explanation: The word 'because' links the blank to the sentence before it: the women 'had never worked a shuttle.' The result clause says they had no old hand-loom habits to undo. The blank therefore has to name a lack of experience, and 'inexperienced in' is that relationship.

A.why: You described the weavers the mills chose not to hire. The recruits had never worked a shuttle, so 'proficient in' reverses what the passage says about them.

C.why: You picked a strong feeling that fits the topic of machines replacing a trade. But the passage says nothing about how the recruits felt. The causal logic is about having no habits to undo, which is a matter of experience, not resentment.

D.why: Devotion to a craft would mean long practice and attachment to it. That clashes with recruits who had never worked a shuttle, and it gives no reason why supervisors had no old habits to undo.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Many Japanese woodblock prints of the Edo period were the work of three specialists: a designer, a carver, and a printer. Art historians once credited the designer alone and treated the carver as a mere copyist. Close study of surviving blocks complicates that view. Carvers were evidently highly ______ the medium's limits, quietly simplifying lines that a designer had drawn too fine for cherry wood to hold.
explanation: The phrase 'complicates that view' tells you the blank sits on the side that overturns the idea of the carver as a mere copyist. The example that follows shows carvers spotting lines too fine for the wood and adjusting them. That shows a skilled awareness of what the medium can do, which is what 'attuned to' means.

A.why: You picked a vivid emotional reaction to the wood's limits. The blocks show that carvers adjusted the lines, not how they felt while doing it. The passage is about skill and awareness, and it gives no evidence of frustration.

B.why: Carvers who did not know the medium's limits could not have spotted which lines the wood would fail to hold. This is the opposite of what the surviving blocks show.

D.why: Carvers simplified the lines to fit the wood, which means they worked within its limits rather than against them. 'Opposed to' reverses that, and it doesn't make sense as a stance toward a physical property of wood.
